questions.q: Identify the two supporting characters who appear in BOTH prose excerpts (जयदेव and मैथिलीशरण गुप्त) but are absent from the poem "हरि-केसव की प्रीति".
questions.a: Correct answer: यशोदा (Krishna's foster mother) and रोहिणी/बलराम की माता (implied in second excerpt). A wrong answer like "राधा" or "गोपियाँ" reveals the student cannot distinguish between the poem's characters (Hari/Kesav) and the prose excerpts' characters. This confusion stems from not separating the three distinct literary pieces in the chapter.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the author (जयदेव/मैथिलीशरण गुप्त) chooses to show Krishna's hunger through Yashoda's eyes rather than Krishna's own perspective.
questions.a: Correct answer: Yashoda's limited human perspective (worry, inability to comprehend divine nature) creates dramatic irony — the reader knows Krishna is divine, but Yashoda sees only a hungry child. This contrast heightens the theme of लीला (divine play). A wrong answer like "to show mother's love" is incomplete; it misses the structural function of dramatic irony and the thematic purpose of contrasting human vs divine vision.

questions.q: In the second prose excerpt (मैथिलीशरण गुप्त), Yashoda sends Krishna to Vrindavan. Using the PEEL structure, write ONE analytical paragraph (4-5 sentences) proving this action makes her a CATALYST for the plot.
questions.a: Sample PEEL response: Point — Yashoda acts as a catalyst by forcing Krishna's departure. Evidence — She says "जा व्रज, देख अपने भूखे बालकों को" (Go to Vraj, see your hungry children). Explanation — This command initiates Krishna's physical journey to Vrindavan, shifting the setting from domestic space to pastoral लीला-ground. Link — Without her intervention, the narrative would remain static in Gokul; her maternal anxiety becomes the divine instrument for लीला's expansion. A wrong answer merely narrates the event without labeling the narrative function (catalyst) or using the term "dramatic agency".

questions.q: Compare the portrayal of maternal anxiety in Yashoda (prose excerpt 1) vs. the implied mother-figure in the poem "हरि-केसव की प्रीति". How does the GENRE (prose vs poetry) change the depiction?
questions.a: Correct answer: Prose (जयदेव) uses detailed narration — Yashoda's internal monologue, physical actions (चूल्हा जलाना, खोजना) — creating realistic, sustained anxiety. Poetry (रसखान) compresses it into lyrical intensity: "तूहीं फटु उकफ्क फुड ल्कप" — the mother's love is expressed through metaphor and rhythm, not narrative detail. A wrong answer lists similarities only ("both show love") ignoring how prose's expansive syntax vs poetry's condensed imagery shape the reader's emotional access.

questions.q: Evaluate this student claim: "Rohini (Balram's mother) is a flat character because she has no dialogues in either excerpt." Defend or refute using textual evidence.
questions.a: Refute. Flatness ≠ silence. Rohini functions as a thematic foil: her absence from dialogue contrasts with Yashoda's vocal anxiety, symbolizing the unseen, steadfast support behind divine missions. In the second excerpt, her implied presence (बलराम सहित) enables Krishna's journey — she releases Balram too. A wrong answer accepts the claim, confusing "flat" (lack of complexity) with "minor" (less page time). This reveals inability to distinguish character *role* from character *depth*.

questions.q: Create a 4-line dialogue between Yashoda and Rohini that could be inserted into the second prose excerpt, revealing their contrasting attitudes toward Krishna's departure. Use vocabulary from the text (e.g., व्रज, लीला, माया).
questions.a:
Good answer example:
यशोदा: "व्रज भेजती हूँ कन्हैया को, मन काँपता है माया से।"
रोहिणी: "लीला है यह हरि की, बहन! बलराम संग जाएँगे दोनों।"
यशोदा: "भूखे बालक रोते द्वार, माँ का हृदय न समझे पार।"
रोहिणी: "जो पालत है जगत सारा, उसकी माँ तू, क्यों घबराई रे?"
Criteria: Uses text vocabulary, shows contrast (anxiety vs faith), maintains character voices. Poor answer: generic modern Hindi dialogue without textual vocabulary or thematic contrast.
